questions.question: Molecular station: melting curve analysis for HHV-6 and CMV.
questions.question_raw: Molecular station: Melting curves (HHV6 and CMV).

parts.text: Sample A had two peaks (one for each virus), but controls were shown only for CMV. How would you report this?
Sample B had a peak for CMV only. How would you report this?

parts_raw.text: Sample A had 2 peaks (1 for each virus) but the controls were only shown for CMV. Asked how to report.
Sample B had a peak for CMV only. Report.

questions.model_answer:
a) Report the CMV result only — CMV is detected and is valid because its positive and negative controls performed acceptably. The HHV-6 peak cannot be reported: without an HHV-6 positive control on the run the melting temperature cannot be verified and the assay is uncontrolled for that target. Report "CMV DNA detected; HHV-6 result pending/invalid — repeat with appropriate HHV-6 controls" and re-run the specimen for HHV-6 with a full control set.
b) Report "CMV DNA detected, HHV-6 DNA not detected" — a single peak at the CMV melting temperature with valid CMV controls; quantify or send for viral load if clinically indicated.

cohort_answer.text: Sample A: report CMV because controls were fine; re-run HHV6 with controls. Sample B: report CMV.

questions.question: A bone marrow transplant patient has fever and HHV-6 is detected in the blood.
questions.question_raw:
Q36 (2003 PM)
Fever in a BMT patient, find HHV-6 in the blood

parts.text: What are the clinical manifestations of HHV-6 infection?
What childhood illness is associated with HHV-6?

parts_raw.text: A. What are the clinical manifestations of HHV-6 infection?
C. What childhood illness is associated with HHV-6?

questions.model_answer:
a) Immunocompetent host: (1) Exanthem subitum (roseola infantum) in young children; (2) Infectious mononucleosis-like illness in older patients (fever, lymphadenopathy, generalized rash, atypical lymphocytes); (3) Association with mesial temporal lobe epilepsy/sclerosis; less commonly hepatitis, myocarditis, thrombocytopenic purpura, hemophagocytic syndrome. Immunocompromised/transplant host: (1) Fever and rash early after transplant; (2) Limbic encephalitis (especially cord blood recipients; headache, confusion, short-term memory loss, insomnia, seizures) and myelitis; (3) Bone marrow suppression/delayed engraftment, and association with pneumonitis, hepatitis, GI disease, and graft-versus-host disease.
b) Supportive care only for most immunocompetent disease (no proven antiviral benefit). HHV-6 is sensitive in vitro to ganciclovir, foscarnet, and cidofovir (foscarnet and cidofovir more active), but NOT acyclovir. For immunocompromised patients with HHV-6 encephalitis, full-dose ganciclovir (>=10 mg/kg) or foscarnet (>=180 mg/kg), or the combination, is recommended; full-dose therapy gives a better response than lower doses. Routine antiviral prophylaxis is not recommended.
c) Exanthem subitum (roseola infantum).

cohort_answer.text:
A: Immunocompetent host: Roseola infantum (exanthem subitum), Mono-like symptoms, Encephalitis, Mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (Associated). Transplant: Pneumonitis, Hepatitis, Myelitis, Limbic Encephalitis (from transplanted cord blood), BM suppression, Associated with graft rejection

B: No therapy. Ganciclovir or foscarnet for immunocompromised with limbic encephalitis

C: Roseola infantum
